editorial:
If you love fairy tales with a modern twist, this movie is a total treat. Giselle is a sweet princess who gets pushed out of her cartoon kingdom and lands in real New York City. The city is loud, messy, and nothing like her storybook home. She meets Robert, a practical lawyer who helps her, and sparks fly even though she is engaged to Prince Edward. The mix of animated magic and real-world chaos keeps things lively and funny. Amy Adams is wonderful as Giselle, bringing big heart and charm to every scene. The songs are catchy, the costumes are bright, and the romance feels warm without being too heavy.

The pacing is quick, the jokes land well, and the supporting cast adds plenty of laughs. Some parts feel a little silly, and the ending is very neat, but that fits the fairy-tale mood. It is great for families, date nights, or anyone wanting a feel-good movie. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Queen Narissa turns into a dragon and tries to kill Giselle and Robert. Giselle uses her bravery and a sword to defeat the queen, saving everyone. Robert and Giselle kiss, breaking the spell and proving true love can be real. Prince Edward returns to Andalasia with Nancy, who becomes his princess. Giselle stays in New York, opens a fashion boutique, and lives happily ever after with Robert and his daughter Morgan.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fairy tales, musicals, and light romantic comedies.
